tagline: Providing managed healthcare services to underserved populations under Medicaid and Medicare programs
hero_kpi_rationale: The MCR is the master KPI in managed healthcare services: it directly measures the ability to control medical costs, the primary risk and profitability driver. For MOH, with Medicaid as the dominant segment, it is the structural profitability driver #1.

kpis.name: Medical Care Ratio
kpis.explanation: Share of medical costs in premium revenues: the lower it is, the higher the margin.
kpis.description: Consolidated MCR increased from 89.1% in 2024 to 91.7% in 2025, a deterioration of 260 basis points, driven by higher healthcare utilization and acuity changes exceeding expectations.
kpis.signal: Deterioration of 260 basis points in 2025, above long-term target

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated by the company over the year.
kpis.description: Total revenue reached $45.4 billion in 2025, up 12% from 2024, driven by the ConnectiCare acquisition, Medicaid rate increases, and Marketplace growth.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income declined to $472 million in 2025 from $1.179 billion in 2024, due to pressure on medical costs and higher interest charges.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in net income of 60%

kpis.name: Pre-tax Margin
kpis.explanation: Profit before taxes divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Pre-tax margin declined from 3.9% in 2024 to 1.3% in 2025, reflecting pressure on medical margins and overhead costs, with a critical compression ratio.

kpis.name: G&A Ratio
kpis.explanation: General and administrative expenses as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: G&A ratio improved slightly to 6.6% in 2025 from 6.7% in 2024, thanks to operational efficiency gains, operating leverage from growth, and reduced performance-based compensation.
kpis.signal: Slight improvement in fixed costs through operating leverage

kpis.name: Member Count
kpis.explanation: Total number of insured members at year-end.
kpis.description: Member count remained stable at 5.5 million at end of 2025, despite Medicaid member losses from redeterminations (4.57M vs 4.89M in 2024), offset by Marketplace growth (655K vs 403K) and the ConnectiCare acquisition.
kpis.signal: Stability despite Medicaid redeterminations and market contraction

kpis.name: Interest Expense
kpis.description: Interest expense increased from $118M in 2024 to $192M in 2025, due to bond issuances ($750M November 2024, $850M November 2025) and temporary borrowings under credit facilities.
kpis.signal: Sharp increase in financial charges due to debt issuances

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the past 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €15.56 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Florida Contract Revenue
kpis.explanation: Expected annual revenues from the new Medicaid contract in Florida.
kpis.description: The Florida contract, awarded in November 2025, will cover approximately 120,000 members and is expected to generate $6 billion in annual Medicaid and CHIP premium revenues, starting Q4 2026.
kpis.signal: Strategic $6B contract in Florida, launch Q4 2026

kpis.name: New Market Wins Revenue
kpis.explanation: Additional annual revenues generated by new Medicaid contracts won in 2025.
kpis.description: New RFPs won in 2025 (Florida, Wisconsin MyChoice LTSS, Georgia and Texas Star+CHIP) collectively represent more than $9 billion in additional annual Medicaid premium revenues.
kpis.signal: $9B in additional annual revenues in growth pipeline

risks.title: Medical costs
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned multiple times in the 10-K (Item 1A Risk Factors and MD&A), with high language intensity regarding insufficient premium rates relative to medical cost increases, and uncertainty surrounding utilization and cost trends. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the 10-K regarding increasing competition in the managed healthcare and Medicaid contract market. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on government contracts
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly addressed in Item 1A Risk Factors: the majority of revenues come from Medicaid and Medicare contracts. The risk of non-renewal or contract loss is substantial. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Liquidity and credit risks
risks.score_rationale: Interest expense increased 63% in 2025 due to bond issuances and borrowings, reflecting a rise in financial leverage. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Operational risks related to integration
risks.score_rationale: The closing of the ConnectiCare acquisition in February 2025 and the growing acquisition pipeline introduce operational integration and execution risks. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Reputation and compliance
risks.score_rationale: The managed healthcare sector is highly regulated and reputation risks related to coverage decisions and quality of care are significant. (default score, to be refined)
